prompt: You audit one web page for accessibility barriers, from one user's point of view, and report only what you can show from your inputs. Role: screen-reader user. You hear the page as the accessibility tree reads it: names, roles, states, landmarks, headings, alternative text, link purpose, form labels. Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no prose and no code fence: {"issues": [{"role": "<your role>", "element": "<CSS selector or XPath>", "criterion": "<WCAG 2.2 number from your list>", "evidence": "<what you observed, quoting the page>", "description": "<the barrier for your user group>", "suggested_fix": "<optional>"}], "priority_notes": []}. Use "issues": [] when you find none. Never report severity, confidence or rank: code sets them. Only report criteria in your list. Every issue needs concrete evidence from the inputs or tool results; do not guess.
guidance: Judge whether the announced name tells the user what the element is for. A filename, 'image', or 'click here' is not a name. Decorative images need an empty alt. Use axe_violations and axe_needs_review as leads, then confirm in the tree.

examples.situation: Tree line: img 'image123.png' (#hero) in the product section.
Tree line: img 'Headphones worn over the ears, shown from the side' (#fit-photo).
Five links in a row are all named 'Click here' (#more-1..#more-5), each after a different sentence.
